changelog:
  - 0.63.0: **owner decision of 2026-10-26** (option B; ANDROID-PLAN
    0.1.83, IOS-PLAN 0.1.37). §11.14.6 "A phone that could not tell",
    "Pairing": a repeated open whose step 2 was stored sets the
    invitation again from the current registration when it is for the
    same identity (the same `ik`; the current `recovery_id` as `ctx`, its
    attestation binding, KEM and relay key), and keeps another
    identity's (E's); so for N the binding after pairing is that of the
    registration whose open answered `ok`. Either way the repeat renews
    the invitation and drops a begun handshake, also E's when N opens,
    as "A lost `ok`" does. The header keeps a recovered phone's earlier
    binding only for the same attested key. Accepted gap: a repeat whose
    header write fails after its state is stored leaves the new key's
    lost-ok unlock refused (`attestation`) until the phone opens again
    while the recovery is registered; an unlock with the earlier key
    then binds the new one. "Outcomes" and "A lost `ok`" follow. No wire
    or API change. **Requires the vault release that carries
    vettid-vault #150 (release 23)**
  - 0.62.1: editorial and clarifying (ANDROID-PLAN 0.1.82, IOS-PLAN 0.1.36);
    no rule of the vault changes. §11.14.6 "Two identities at most": the
    contact text's action reads "Email support@vettid.org" (owner
    decision of 2026-10-26), and the texts `recover_other_vault` and
    `recover_undecided_new_code`, as Android words them, are quoted as
    approved by the owner on 2026-10-26. "A failed register": a register
    POST is judged on its own, not once per register flow, and is
    recorded before it is posted; the answers that mean "got no `202`"
    are listed in full, and only a first such POST counts as not
    registered; a failure after a `202` (the poll fails, times out,
    answers `retry`, or shows the slot status `expired`) means maybe
    registered, confirmed with the status signed with K; a readable
    refusal settles its POST as not registered; a re-post of the same
    code after a request whose slot showed `expired` is a repeat; retries
    with the same N, K and code are always allowed; a `401` drops only
    an N that never had a registration answered `ok`, left maybe
    registered, or unknown. No wire change, no API change
  - 0.62.0: **owner decisions of 2026-10-25**; the contact text was approved
    by the owner on 2026-10-26 (MEMBER-API 2.13.0 unchanged, ANDROID-PLAN
    0.1.81, IOS-PLAN 0.1.35). §11.14.6 "A phone that could not tell",
    new "Two identities at most": at most two device identities (the
    earlier and one new), never a third; further recoveries reuse the
    new one (owner D1); if its recovery also ends, the phone keeps both and keeps trying the lost-ok
    unlock (newest, then earlier), and after a day of refusals shows a
    contact text (not "Your vault took this phone"); a recovery code for
    another vault is refused as soon as the claim or register names it;
    one App Attest key per identity; the two status reads (wall and
    monotonic clock, 5 minutes, agreeing within 2); what a day of refusals
    counts; a failed register is retried with the same new identity, and a `401` drops it; the
    codes that prove no step 1 settle only their own open; each open's
    history is saved before it is posted; pairing by each identity's own
    `recovery_id`. No wire change, no API change
  - 0.61.0: editorial (with VAULT-HOST-PROTOCOL 0.1.16; as built in
    vettid-vault #149, main 1347c87; owner decision of 2026-10-25). The
    parent's confirmations of the app key (the acknowledged request of
    §11.5, §11.14.2, including the enrollment's) are made only by the
    instance that holds the vault's unexpired lease, and the enclave
    confirms the next key again once step 1 is stored; the clear of a key
    a failed step 1 left on the row is bound to the clearing parent's own
    confirmation and to the lease, and none is sent when step 1 loses to
    another instance. §11.5's enrollment wording is corrected to say so.
    No wire change, no change for the apps
  - 0.60.0: **owner decision of 2026-10-24**; the code and the times are
    proposed for the owner's approval (MEMBER-API 2.13.0, built in
    vettid.org, not deployed; ANDROID-PLAN 0.1.79, IOS-PLAN 0.1.34). It
    rests on vettid-vault #148 (main 276a23a; 0.58.0 above,
    VAULT-HOST-PROTOCOL 0.1.15 §5.7): the row names every key the vault
    adopted, as `app_key` or `app_key_next`, before the vault stores a
    header that names it. §11.14.6, new "A recovery that ended without
    the phone": the member API answers a request signed by a recovering
    key whose recovery ended without the vault adopting the phone with
    **`410 recovery_ended`** (from one hour to 30 days after the end,
    judged by the key's latest end), and still `401` for every other
    failure. **The rule for apps**: on `recovery_ended` the phone may
    forget its pending (recovering) key and offer to start over **only
    if it has never been admitted as the app (no `ok`, token or vault
    bundle) and has no unanswered open**; a phone that has ever been
    admitted treats it as a `401`, and one with an unanswered open keeps
    K and follows "A phone that could not tell" (the exact orphan clear
    of #148 can remove `app_key_next` while the vault's header still
    names K). On `401` it never forgets. The 410-versus-401 difference
    is an accepted leak; the residuals (split brain, a dishonest parent)
    are named. A `200` (admitted as the app) is not proof of adoption
    ("A phone that could not tell"). §11.11.7 "Claim" points there, and
    no longer says the recovering key may `unlock` and `lock` (refused
    since 0.33.0, MEMBER-API 2.7.0/2.10.1). No vault change, no wire
    change in the enclave
  - 0.59.0: **owner decisions of 2026-10-24** (option A; a key in use
    is `app_key` or a live `app_key_pending`, never `app_key_next`);
    with MEMBER-API 2.12.0 (built in vettid.org, not deployed),
    ANDROID-PLAN 0.1.78 and IOS-PLAN 0.1.33; no vault release, no wire
    change. §11.14.6, new "A phone that could not tell": a registered
    phone whose open was sent and never answered readably, whose
    recovery has since ended, MAY be used for a new recovery of the
    same vault with the same recovering key K, when status with K
    answers `401` (or `410 recovery_ended`, once the member API gives
    it), or answers `200` and the phone's unlock is answered
    `transfer_incomplete` (the state still under `DEK_0`). It deletes
    nothing; it registers a new identity (`device_ik`, `kem`, relay key)
    with K, and its open carries the `unlock_secret` of the earlier
    open, which a vault whose step 1 of the order of writes is stored
    requires (§11.14.2, `device_secret` otherwise). The member API
    refuses a claim with a key in use (`409 key_in_use`) and never
    records one as the recovering key, so that the reuse cannot
    complete the new recovery falsely. A `200` alone is not proof of
    adoption (`app_key_next` can stay after an open that stopped); only
    K as `app_key`, an unlock answered `ok` or a completed handshake is.
    The phone keeps every identity's `recovery_id` as its handshake
    context (`hs.init` is looked up by `ctx`). The outcomes, and what
    the phone keeps until the vault answers `ok` and the pairing
    completes
  - 0.58.0: **durable app key writes** (with VAULT-HOST-PROTOCOL 0.1.15;
    as built in vettid-vault #148, main 276a23a; for the owner's
    approval). Whenever the vault has adopted an app key, the vault row
    names it as `app_key` or `app_key_next`, durably. §11.5: the parent
    writes `app_key_next` on the row **before the vault stores the
    header that names it**, in an acknowledged request
    (VAULT-HOST-PROTOCOL §5.7); the lifecycle event `app_key_next` is only
    a report. The writes of `app_key` and `app_key_next` are conditional on
    `seq` and `header_seq`, and a failed one is written again until it is
    written; `app_key` and the removal of `app_key_next` are one write; the
    enclave tells the parent its app key state again after every hello.
    §11.14.2: the confirmation comes before step 1 (a replacement does
    not begin without the parent's `ok`), and before any other header that
    names an app key the stored header does not (a replacement resumed at
    an unlock, the first header at enrollment, a change outside a
    replacement); the next key a failed step 1 left on the row is cleared
    at once (`app_key_next_clear`); `next_cleared` removes `app_key_next`
    only if its `header_seq` is not above the event's. The release R list
    of chosen names adds `AppKeyNext` and the assertion of the current
    key. A dishonest parent can still cause a refusal of the phone (by
    answering `ok` without writing or by rewriting the row): availability
    only. No change for the apps
  - 0.57.0: **owner decisions of 2026-10-24** (with MEMBER-API 2.11.0,
    ANDROID-PLAN 0.1.77, IOS-PLAN 0.1.32). §12.5 new **"What a phone
    does"**: a phone erases its local vault data because of a deletion
    only on a definite answer, never on a `401`. Automatic erase only
    with **both** (a) the vault's own sealed word
    (`device.unlinked{vault_deleted}`, or the `{}` answer to this
    phone's own `vault.delete`) **and** (b) the member API's
    authenticated `410 vault_deleted` or `410 account_deleted`. With
    one of them alone the phone keeps checking (the status, and with
    (b) alone also its own relay mailbox for the vault's event) and, in
    both cases after the same 10-minute bound, offers a confirmed
    **Remove from this phone** (with (b) alone it shows "Your vault was
    deleted"). The `410` answers an authenticated request; the answer
    itself is protected by TLS only. Everything else (`401`, `{vault: null}`, `403`, `5xx`,
    timeouts) is "could not tell" and erases nothing. The member API
    keeps the record of a removed deleted vault 90 days (MEMBER-API
    "Vault deletion", What a phone is told), so (b) stays available
    after the row is gone. §12.5 "What the member API shows meanwhile"
    and §11.5 corrected: a `deleted` row read `{vault: null}` to the
    portal's session only; apps were answered `401`, and from MEMBER-API
    2.11.0 `410`. §11.5's table lists the record and the vault row's
    `account_deleted_at`. The vault-sealed per-device deletion proof is
    later. No wire change in the vault
  - 0.56.4: editorial (aligns §10.2 with VAULT-LOCK §3.5/§3.7, MEMBER-API
    "Locks" and ANDROID-PLAN part 2; found in the review of
    vettid-android #190). §10.2 "Locks": `stale_lock` was listed among
    what a device may take as confirmation that the vault is locked,
    against the bullet that says it means the vault is open under a
    newer unlock. It ends the device's lock without confirming it; the
    device does not repeat it on its own, but the member's own new lock
    (the "Lock it now" button, owner decision 2026-10-24) is allowed;
    the device reads the status. A device with no current `unlock_id`
    handles a `vault.locking` by the time rule. No wire change
  - 0.56.3: editorial; from the independent review of vettid-vault #147
    (release L, V2), as built there. §11.5 "The `lock` operation": an
    unconditional lock against a vault whose opening has no known
    `enqueued_at` is carried out (locking only reduces exposure); and a
    known residual: an unlock queued before an unconditional lock (the
    account site's) but delivered after it still opens the vault, since
    the queue is not ordered and a message can arrive up to 5 minutes
    late. The opening needs the PIN, and the idle lock (§3.6.8) bounds
    how long it stays open. No rule changes
  - 0.56.2: approved by the owner 2026-10-23. §11.14.10 rule 5 and §6.7.1
    (failure row "The new app goes offline after its `hs.fin`"): at its
    11-minute deadline the new app of a transfer **collects its mailbox
    once** before it drops its handshake, attested key and epoch-1 secret;
    a `device.paired{transfer}` for this transfer, opened under its
    session, is applied and the move completes. ANDROID-PLAN 0.1.76.
  - 0.56.1: **owner decisions of 2026-10-23** (§3.6.8: keep the
    shorter; a call delays the idle lock at most 12 hours; no extra hour
    for an unlock before the idle lock's time) and editorial errata
    (owner answers on the release L plan, VAULT-LOCK 0.1.3 Q1, Q3; the
    unlock_id part as in vettid-vault #145 (open); the enqueued_at
    ordering is not built yet (V2)). §10.2 "Locks", §11.5 "The `lock` operation": a **recovery
    open is an opening of the vault**: it makes an `unlock_id` (already
    a member of `vault.recovery.open.result`, §11.14.6, which releases
    from R to L sent empty), and an unconditional lock is compared with
    the `enqueued_at` of the `recovery_open` message as with an enroll's
    or an unlock's. §8.6: a device that implements 0.29.0 but does not
    hold the value of a vault that announced one (an install from before
    that version, a lost record) locks as for a vault before L over the
    relay (once, the wait before its next unlock), and through the
    member API without the value (an unconditional lock). §11.14.10:
    if the old app's renewal of its token before an approval fails, it
    still sends the approval, and the notice has what the previous token
    has left (as in vettid-vault #144, open). §3.6.8: (owner decision
    2026-10-23, "keep the shorter") the lowest idle-lock value set since
    the last check stays in force until the next one, and a call in
    progress delays the idle lock at most 12 hours past its time (a
    call ends within 12 hours, §10.10), and an unlock before the idle
    lock's time gets no extra hour, as in vettid-vault #146 (open,
    97d309f);
    an editorial note that "shortening may lock the vault at once" has
    no effect (the setting cannot change past the deadline). No other
    rule changes
  - 0.56.0: **draft; the owner answered the proposed choices on 2026-10-23, the
    text awaits approval** (the owner decided on 2026-10-23 to specify and build wallet spend caps before
    the Android wallet work, W1 and W2); ANDROID-PLAN 0.1.74,
    STAGING-TIME-SCALE 0.1.4. **A vault change** (vettid-vault
    `features/wallet`), with a release, and new app screens. The
    requirement is VAULT-PLAN V4 "Wallet note" and PROTEAN-CREDENTIAL §5
    ("member-set **spend caps** per transaction and per period ... enforced
    by the vault before it signs, with raising a cap a credential
    operation (password, CEK rotation) and every refusal audited";
    "**spend caps** (`max_amount`) are a requirement for the wallet
    batch"). §10.18 "Spend caps": per wallet, in sats, a maximum per
    transaction and a maximum per rolling 24 hours (the period); none
    by default, which the app asks about at creation; what counts is
    what leaves the wallet in a signed PSBT (payees and fee, change
    excluded); checked after the PSBT checks and before the password is
    tried; `cap_exceeded` with `{reason, limit_sats, ...}`; audit kinds
    `wallet.cap_refused`, `wallet.caps_lowered`, `wallet.caps_raised`,
    never an amount. **Owner decisions of 2026-10-23:** no caps by default,
    the app asks at creation and a mainnet wallet cannot skip the question; raising or removing a cap takes the
    PIN and the password; so does revealing the phrase of a wallet that
    has caps (`item.reveal`, `pin_required`); a rolling 24 hours only
    (VAULT-PLAN V4 said "per day, per week"). Review fixes: the check's
    place in §3.5.3, the clock rule, atomic check-and-append, fee bumps
    counted in full, rollback, `exists` for a duplicate import,
    `cap` in `wallet.psbt.inspect`, the `payload_sha256` encoding and a
    vector. New messages: `wallet.caps.set` (a normal change,
    lowering only) and `wallet.caps.raise` (a credential operation with
    the PIN and the password, bound to the new values). `wallet.create`
    may carry `caps`; `<wallet>` carries `caps`. The period is divided
    by `time_scale` on staging (STAGING-TIME-SCALE S17). Stated plainly:
    a cap limits what the vault signs, not what `item.reveal` of the
    phrase lets a person do elsewhere (§10.18). Tests required.
  - 0.55.10: **decisions approved by the owner
    (2026-10-23)** (five: the three below, the notice's reliability and
    the waiting notice's text), found in the iOS review (claude-mac) and
    the independent review; ANDROID-PLAN 0.1.72, IOS-PLAN 0.1.31,
    STAGING-TIME-SCALE 0.1.3, RUNBOOK. No change to the wire format;
    **vault changes for release L (staging release 23)**, plus the old
    app renewing the vault's deposit token at the approval. §11.14.10:
    (1) the old phone no longer erases at its first start 7 days after
    the approval; at or after day 7 it asks its vault (`device.list`)
    first, and a vault that does not answer (locked, `lock_pending`, a
    timeout, offline) is "not known: check again later", never an
    erase; it erases only on `device.unlinked{transferred}` or on a
    definite answer that it is no longer the vault's app, and a
    cancelled or interrupted check never erases; the residual (a vault
    that never answers keeps the old keys on the phone) is stated;
    (2) the app re-reads its transfer record after the check's await and
    records "kept, not done" only if that write succeeded, else the
    check runs again; (3) the new phone waits 11 minutes, not 10, for
    the approval (§6.7, §6.7.1); (4) the notice is reliable: the old app
    renews the vault's standing deposit token when it approves, so the
    token has its full 30 days; the vault keeps the pending unlink for
    that token's life (no 7-day expiry), keeps the old session's sending
    key and seals `device.unlinked{transferred}` at delivery (so §8.4's
    16 days do not cut it short), at the vault's current app's first
    unlock from storage; (5) the waiting notice reads "Your vault has not
    confirmed the move to this phone. Once your new phone opens your
    vault, remove VettID from this phone." Also: result 2 (the vault
    answers and the phone is still its app: no erase, the keep ends);
    `token_revoked` is read as no answer (§8.6); what a removed phone
    hears; what counts as a definite answer; the generation rule for
    recording the check. IOS-PLAN §14: the text for a signer change on
    an iPhone to Android move.
  - 0.55.9: editorial; **two decisions approved by the owner
    (2026-10-23)**, on the independent review's advice; as built in
    vettid-vault #142 (IOS-PLAN 0.1.30, VA4). §11.7.1 "Across an iOS
    app" is no longer "decided, not implemented": the vault keeps the
    last recorded Android signer (digest and class) while its app has
    none, including across iOS to iOS moves, and clears it when the
    binding moves to an Android app. The vault's signer binding is the
    app's recorded signer, or the kept signer while the app has none;
    the kept signer counts as recorded for `signer_changed`, so Android
    S1, iOS, Android S2 is `signer_changed: true` and is confirmed and
    audited as between two Android apps, in a transfer and in a
    recovery (release R's open and the recovered phone's pairing, a
    resumed recovery open included). **(q1) A return to the same signer
    as the kept one is audited `device.signer_bound`, with no
    confirmation and no `signer_changed`.** **(q2) The kept signer is
    stored in the vault's DEK-encrypted state (`kept_signer`), as
    `recovered_signer` is, not in the sealed header's device
    bindings;** its freshness is `recovered_signer`'s. A kept signer
    the running release no longer pins is never checked at unlock; a
    later return to Android is `signer_changed` with the kept class.
    `device.list` does not show it; audit and feed carry classes only.
    Stale text fixed: the "Across platforms" bullet, the `signer_changed`
    definition, `signer_unconfirmed` spends the UTK (0.52.0), "not yet implemented" in the
    0.27.1 entries, and the "stranded vaults" paragraph (the kept-signer
    case). New tests required (VA4). Header reference to ANDROID-PLAN
    brought up to 0.1.71. Corrections found in review: recovery is
    release R's open and the recovered phone's first handshake
    (`credential.recover` is removed), and the open records
    `recovered_signer` rather than moving the binding (§11.7.1,
    §11.14.6)
  - 0.55.8: editorial; one new device rule: `keySize` exactly 128 or
    256 (§10.10 "Media suites"); library facts confirmed on two phones
    (2026-10-23; vettid-android #175; CALLING-SERVICE 0.2.2, CALLS-PLAN
    0.1.5), awaiting the owner's approval; no protocol change. §10.10
    "Media suites": the media stack in use is now
    `io.github.webrtc-sdk:android:150.7871.04` (AAR SHA-256
    `1872dda4…9c84c`), which carries upstream PR #302: the key
    provider takes `keySize` in bits, and only 128 and 256 mean what
    they say (any other value is silently 128 **[S]**). Suite 2's
    state is now "the stack can do it"; its derivation (L = 32) and
    frame format are confirmed against that release **[D]**, and its
    frame key in the vectors is no longer provisional. Suite 2 is
    still **not offered or chosen in form 1** ("Call forms", rules 1
    and 3), only once form 1 is retired. Also written down: the sizes must match
    or the frame fails (`DECRYPTION_FAILED`); for one `k_dir` the
    16-byte key is the first half of the 32-byte one, which is
    harmless; the ratchet's output length (unused: window 0); the
    library's key logging (INFO up to `.01`, sizes only at VERBOSE
    from `.04`; the rule stands); `uncryptedMagicBytes` from `.04`
  - 0.55.7: editorial; **approved by the owner (2026-10-23)** (from the
    independent review of the iOS app's share-question handling; the
    Android app had the same three differences). §10.12 "Listing
    pending decisions": new "Share questions that change while the app
    reads the lists" (apps MUST): (1) a decision drops an item of a
    `share.pending` batch only if it was made after that batch arrived;
    (2) a question the read covers but does not list keeps only the
    items of the batches that arrived after the read began, and goes
    when none are left; (3) a question dropped on `not_found` also
    loses its logged batches. Recorded as open, not a rule: two
    overlapping reads that finish out of order. 0.55.6 was not used:
    PR #400 became 0.55.8;
    ANDROID-PLAN, IOS-PLAN unchanged
  - 0.55.5: editorial; **approved by the owner (2026-10-22)**
    (ANDROID-PLAN 0.1.70, IOS-PLAN 0.1.28). §10.7 "Canonical forms",
    `date`: a month field (a stored `YYYY-MM`, or a new or empty field
    whose template has `"format": "month"`, such as a card's expiry)
    refuses any invalid value, a full date typed or pasted there
    included, with its own message, "Enter a month and year, such as
    2033-05" (`items_rule_month`), instead of the date message; day
    fields keep theirs
  - 0.55.4: editorial; **approved by the owner (2026-10-22)**
    (ANDROID-PLAN 0.1.69, IOS-PLAN 0.1.27; from the comparison of
    73,000 inputs between the two apps). §10.7 "Phone values": (1)
    **no silent digit cut**: digits are not cut to 15 before parsing;
    the library decides: a number it finds `IS_POSSIBLE` is stored in
    E.164 whatever its length, and only `TOO_LONG` or another result
    that is not possible takes the fallback, its dialable characters (a
    `+` typed before the first digit, then all its digits). Every
    writer keeps the edit text, extension marker included, to at most
    32 characters, so the fallback always fits the table; (2) **"Check this number"** shows whenever the number
    is not valid (`isValidNumber` is false), whether it is stored as
    E.164 or as dialable characters, and never blocks; both apps track
    the current libphonenumber metadata (no pin), since validity can
    change with the metadata
  - 0.55.3: editorial; found in review (the Android review of the
    canonical forms; ANDROID-PLAN 0.1.68, IOS-PLAN 0.1.26). §10.7
    "Canonical forms": (1) `date`: the form of the value already stored;
    a field with no stored value at hand (a new or empty field) takes
    `YYYY-MM` when its template carries `"format": "month"`, else
    `YYYY-MM-DD`; a month-only value typed into a day field is accepted
    as `YYYY-MM`; the app never invents or drops a day (0.55.0 put the
    template's hint first). (2) `url`: a bracketed IPv6 literal is the
    host as a whole, lower-cased, the port after the closing bracket.
    (3) `url`: a text without `://` also keeps its scheme when it looks
    like one (`urn:isbn:1`, `bitcoin:bc1qxyz`, `geo:1,2`), and gets
    `https://` when it looks like a host and port (`localhost:8080/x`,
    `Example.com:443/A`). (4) `number`: the input filter, not the stored
    form, turns a leading `.5` into `0.5` and a decimal comma into a
    point while the member types
  - 0.55.2: editorial; **approved by the owner (2026-10-22)**
    (ANDROID-PLAN 0.1.67, IOS-PLAN 0.1.25). §10.7 "Canonical forms",
    `number`: the stored form is the text as typed, except that leading
    and trailing white space is trimmed and a single leading `+` is
    dropped. Leading zeros, `-0` and trailing fractional zeros are
    kept as typed (`007` stays `007`, `1.0` stays
    `1.0`, `+5` becomes `5`), because members use Number for codes
    such as PINs and account numbers and nothing compares number
    values, so nothing is silently changed. This replaces the 0.55.0
    rule, which dropped leading and trailing zeros. The grammar is
    unchanged and its refusals stand (`5.` and `.5` are refused as
    typed today)
  - 0.55.1: editorial; errata to 0.55.0 found in the Android review
    (ANDROID-PLAN 0.1.66, IOS-PLAN 0.1.24), approved by the owner
    (2026-10-22). §10.7 "Phone values": an extension marker counts only
    when at least one digit comes before it, so "Fax: +44 20 7946 0958"
    and "Text 555 0100" are numbers, not extensions; the edit text keeps
    the exact marker text the member typed (`,123`, `#123`, `ext. 123`)
    until the save; "the `+`" of the rules below is a `+` that comes
    before the first digit, not only one that starts the text. The
    apps' text (ANDROID-PLAN, IOS-PLAN): "N more may be shared" ends
    with a full stop (the apps join it with the other sentences of the
    change text)
  - 0.55.0: normative for the apps; owner decisions of 2026-10-22,
    **approved by the owner (2026-10-22)**. No vault release, no change
    for the member API or the host (the vault validates shape and size
    only); apps: ANDROID-PLAN 0.1.65, IOS-PLAN 0.1.23. (1) **One
    canonical stored form per value kind** (§10.7): a general rule that
    the spec defines the stored form of every value, independent of
    any library's formatting, and apps format only for display. (2)
    **`phone` values** (§10.7): after the extension is dropped, a
    number that parses as a possible number is stored in **E.164**
    (`+442079460958`); any other is stored as its dialable characters
    only (a `+` typed before the first digit, then its digits),
    with the "Check this number" hint and never a block. National,
    international and as-you-type formats are display only. Values already stored in the
    spaced international form (staging) are read and shown, and stored
    again canonically only when the member next edits and saves that
    field; there
    is no bulk migration. A formatted form is not stored because it
    depends on each library's metadata version, so two apps could store
    one number two ways. **An extension is not stored**: the main number
    is, and the app says so while the member types (the extension goes
    in the item's notes). **The other kinds** (§10.7, "Canonical
    forms"): `number`, `date`, `email`, `url`, `otp`, `address` and
    `text` each get one stored form, applied by the apps on save; older
    values are read as before and stored again only when the field is
    next saved. (3) **A truncated preview** (§10.8, `tag.merge`): `shares`
    entries beyond the listed ones are no longer counted as asked; the
    apps say "N more may be shared". An `auto` entry that carries
    `ask_rule_id` counts as asked
  - 0.54.0: normative; owner decisions of 2026-10-21, **approved by the
    owner (2026-10-21)**. **Needs a vault release** for part (1)
    (staging release 21); apps: ANDROID-PLAN 0.1.64, IOS-PLAN 0.1.22
    (a History title); no change for the member API
    or the host. (1) **`credential.holder_cleared`** (§3.5.9, §10.9):
    the pass that clears a holder naming no live app when the state is
    loaded (0.52.0) is audited, `device_id` = the cleared holder's
    device id, nothing secret. Since a removal clears the holder with
    its device, a hit points to a fault or to tampering. History only,
    no feed item, as for the other defensive entries
    (`profile.core_missing`, `device.signer_refused`): the member
    cannot act on it in the feed, and the vault already answers every
    app `no_holder`, which the apps show, and refuses `feed.list`
    until a recovery; the recovered phone then finds the entry in
    History. (2) **`vault.delete` and `no_holder`** (§3.5.7, §3.5.9,
    §10.1, §10.2), as built since 0.52.0: a vault with a credential
    but no holder answers `vault.delete` with `credential_required`
    and body `{"reason": "no_holder"}`. §3.5.9 no longer exempts
    "the types a restricted vault always accepts" as a whole:
    `vault.delete` is among them only before a credential exists (the
    enrolling app's, §12.5, now named in §3.5.7's list), and is the
    holder's afterwards
  - 0.53.0: normative; owner decision of 2026-10-20, **approved by the
    owner (2026-10-20); wording to be confirmed**. **Needs a vault
    release** for part (2) (staging release 21); apps: ANDROID-PLAN
    0.1.59, IOS-PLAN 0.1.17, which ship part (1) independently of the
    vault release; no change for the member API or the host. Found when
    an attestation timestamp about a second behind the enclave's clock
    made clients refuse a valid descriptor: the enclave set `not_after`
    to its own clock + 24 h, and the apps (and the reference client)
    allowed `not_after` at most 24 h + 1 s after the attestation's
    timestamp, an allowance §11.2 never stated, so every unlock into
    that instance failed closed until the ETK rotated. New §11.2
    **"Lifetime and clock allowance"**: (1) **apps** refuse a descriptor
    whose `not_after` is more than **24 h + 5 min** after the
    attestation's timestamp (or not after the app's current time);
    every other check is unchanged; (2) **the enclave** sets `not_after`
    at most **24 h − 60 s** after its own clock, so a correct vault
    never sits at the limit; rotation at 23 h is unchanged, and the
    previous ETK's 1 h grace never runs past its `not_after`. Why this
    is safe is stated there. The descriptor example and step 3 follow
  - 0.52.0: normative; owner decisions of 2026-10-20, **approved by the
    owner (2026-10-20)**. **Needs a vault
    release** (staging release 20); apps: ANDROID-PLAN 0.1.58, IOS-PLAN
    0.1.16; no change for the member API or the host. Found when a
    phone whose daily checks were refused before the key was spent ran
    out of keys for good: the apps drop a UTK when they send it, but
    the vault kept it when it refused the request before the spend, so
    its pool for the phone filled with UTKs the phone no longer had and
    `credential.utk.get` returned none. (1) **Spend first** (§3.5.4
    "Using a UTK"): a request spends the UTK it presents as soon as its
    body parses and its `utk_id` reads, before any other check (a
    recovering app's limits, the holder, transfer and alarm rules, the
    signer confirmation, `unsupported_type`, `credential_required`,
    `owner_check_required`, `session_required`, `forbidden`, the
    features' holder and app-only checks); **a refusal still spends the
    UTK**: a readable `utk_id` in the sender's pool is spent whatever
    the outcome, so an app never puts one back. A body without a
    readable `utk_id` spends nothing. §3.5.3 step 1, §3.5.9 Freeze,
    §3.6.1 step 1, §6.7.1 step 3 (`signer_unconfirmed` now leaves the
    UTK spent), §10.9 (`audit.export`), §10.18 (`wallet.sign`) and
    §11.7.1's tests say so; the earlier "the UTK is not spent" texts
    are replaced. (2) **Resync** (§3.5.4 Pool, §10.6):
    `credential.utk.get{resync: true}` drops the device's pool and
    issues a full pool of 20, at most once per 10 minutes per device
    (divided by `time_scale` on staging, §11.10.8; `too_soon`
    otherwise), audited `credential.utk_resync`; the app sends it only
    when `utk.get` returned no UTKs while its own pool is empty. (3)
    **`no_holder`** (§3.5.7, §3.5.9, §10.1): a vault with a credential
    but no holder answers `credential_required` with body `{"reason":
    "no_holder"}`, also to the holder-only types; `forbidden` to a
    holder-only type now means only that another live app holds the
    credential. (4) **Holder hardening** (§3.5.9, §6.7.1, §11.14.6):
    the holder is none or exactly one live app; removing the holder's
    device clears it; a holder that names no live app is cleared when
    the state is loaded; a recovered phone's first handshake also
    removes every other app; `credential.unlock` is holder-only in the
    vault, as §3.5.9 always said. (5) **No adoption**: the vault still
    never adopts an app as holder; the `no_holder` answer leads the
    apps to a recovery on the account site
  - 0.51.2: clarification, owner decision of 2026-10-20, **approved by
    the owner (2026-10-20)**. No change to what the vault does: no
    vault release, no change for the member API or the host; apps only
    (ANDROID-PLAN 0.1.57, IOS-PLAN 0.1.15). Found when a phone failed
    its daily check with a generic text every time. §10.1: **error
    codes are not secret**; an app may, and should, show a code it does
    not map, and nothing else of the response. **`credential_required`**
    may answer an owner device's request before the type's handler,
    with no UTK spent and nothing tested or counted. **`forbidden`**
    also answers a holder-only type (§3.5.9) from an app that is not
    the holder, and any type outside the recovery path from a
    recovering app
  - 0.51.1: normative clarification, owner decision of 2026-10-20,
    **approved by the owner (2026-10-20)**; found while implementing
    the reset's lost answer on iOS. No vault release, no change for the
    member API or the host; apps only (ANDROID-PLAN 0.1.55, IOS-PLAN
    0.1.13). §11.14.9 **"Another phone became the holder"**: deciding
    an unresolved change or reset ("A lost answer", "A lost answer to
    `credential.reset`") uses calls that only the holder may make. When
    another phone has meanwhile become the holder (a recovery elsewhere,
    a transfer), the vault answers them `forbidden`, which nothing here
    covered, so the app stayed at "can't reach" with the gate closed
    for ever. A `forbidden` answer from the vault to any request of the
    resolution now **ends the unresolved change**: the marker and the
    candidate are cleared, the gate opens, and the app shows its text
    for a vault that moved to another phone. **Only the vault's own
    end-to-end encrypted answer counts**: a transport error, a timeout,
    an HTTP or host failure, or anything else not from the vault stays
    "can't reach", so a faulty or hostile host cannot end a change. It
    is not a proof that this phone was replaced: nothing is erased
  - 0.51.0: normative; **approved by the owner (2026-10-20)**; with
    VAULT-HOST-PROTOCOL 0.1.14 and MEMBER-API 2.10.0 (vettid.org #356).
    **Needs a vault release** (staging release 20: the vault, its
    supervisor and its parent, all in vettid-vault) **and the member
    API**. Apps and account site: no change. §12.5: **a deletion that
    stops between step 1 and step 5 is finished without the app.**
    Until now only an unlock, a recovery request, a registration or a
    cancellation that read the `deleting` header finished it; after
    `device.unlinked{vault_deleted}` the app sends none of them, so a
    crash, a host failure or a store error during steps 2 to 5 left the
    vault listed for ever (the app's "Still finishing"). (A) **The host
    records the deletion before anyone is told** (step 1, new last
    part): after the marking flush the vault asks its parent to mark
    the vault row (`MarkDeleting`, VAULT-HOST-PROTOCOL §5.6), which
    the parent answers only once the row holds `deleting_at`; the
    vault delivers nothing of step 2 (no notice, no answer, no mailbox
    deletion) before that answer, and without it within 2 minutes it
    ends its process locked, with the header marked, so that the
    member's next unlock finishes the deletion as before. (B) **The
    member API resumes a marked deletion** with the new queue
    operation **`delete_resume`** (§11.5): the enclave erases only a
    vault whose own sealed header records `deleting`, or reports
    `deleted` for one whose header and state are both already gone;
    it never erases a vault it can read as live, so the resume is not
    an authority to delete (the authority is the one recorded by the
    sealed marker). (C) **A state that records `deleting` never runs**:
    a crash between the marking flush's state write and its header
    write left a header without the marker, which an unlock opened as
    a vault that handled nothing and could not be deleted from the
    app; such an open now completes the deletion instead. (D) Step 4
    is retried in the process for up to 60 s before the process ends.
    (E) An `unlocked` report clears the row's mark (a vault that runs
    is not being deleted). (F) **The mark stays internal**: it is
    host-written, and the host is not trusted, so the member API uses
    `deleting_at` (and `deletion_resumed_at`) only to send
    `delete_resume`, with its log and metric, and **never shows it**.
    `GET /api/vault/status` keeps the row's own state (no new status
    value), the account site shows no "being deleted" text and keeps
    offering recovery and start-over, and the apps show "being deleted"
    only after the vault's own `device.unlinked{vault_deleted}`; they
    never derive a deletion from the member API's status. A forged or
    stale mark causes at most `delete_resume` requests, which the vault
    ignores unless its own sealed header records `deleting`. §11.5 and
    §12.5 "Convergence" follow
  - 0.50.1: normative correction, approved by the owner (2026-10-20); vault
    PR vettid-vault #132, found by the independent review of #131;
    **needs a vault release** (#132). No
    change for apps, the member API or the host. §11.14.11: **a
    `recovery.attempt` entry is not urgent only if it is in the
    generation of the member's last completed recovery and at or below
    that recovery's own counted attempt *k***; every later attempt is
    `urgent`, also in the same generation. Until now every attempt in
    the recovered generation was taken as the member's, so a later
    recovery by someone else, in the generation the vault stays armed
    in, was audited without urgency. The vault keeps that attempt
    (generation, *k*) in its state; a state from before has only the
    generation, which is no longer read, so its attempts are `urgent`.
    §11.14.2 step 1: for a recovery the `next` part also holds its
    counted attempt (generation, *k*), as the optional sealed field
    `recovery_attempt`. §11.14.6: a repeat whose step 2 was not stored
    takes the attempt from there and sends `Succeed` again (the first
    run's pending success was in the state that was not stored);
    `Succeed` is create-only, so a resend is harmless. A `next` part
    from before has no `recovery_attempt`: its attempt stays `urgent`
    and nothing is resent. §11.14.11: the counter's status read at a
    completion is bounded to 10 seconds; a failure there still answers
    `ok`, and the next owner check writes the entries
  - 0.50.0: normative; approved by the owner (2026-10-19, 2026-10-20)
    with the apps' event titles (ANDROID-PLAN 0.1.52 §4 "Event titles",
    IOS-PLAN 0.1.11 §4.1). **Needs a vault release** for (A) and (B);
    the rest states what vettid-vault `main` (staging release 19) does.
    (A) **`rollback`** (owner decision of 2026-10-20: the vault splits
    the reason): `recovery.generation_closed` gets the reason `rollback`
    for a next generation that already shows used attempts when a change
    is applied, a host serving an older copy of the vault's recovery
    record; it is shown to the member, and makes an `urgent` feed item
    (owner decision of 2026-10-20), on which apps notify on Security
    alarms. `stale` stays for a next
    generation that is only already closed (a retry after a failed
    write), which the apps hide. Today the vault writes `stale` for both.
    (B) **The attempting phone's name stays** (owner decision of
    2026-10-20): the vault records, with each open it notes, the name
    the registering phone gave in `vault.recovery.register`
    (`app.name`, §11.11.3), as a third part of the `recovery.open`
    entry's `ref`; it is self-reported, shown as such, and never affects
    urgency or any decision. Today the vault notes no name, and the
    unmerged 0.49.1 draft that dropped the requirement is withdrawn.
    As built: §10.9 audit kinds: `vault.pin_changed` (a PIN change),
    which the spec did not name, and `recovery.open`,
    `identity.rotate_resolved`, `device.unlinked_sent`,
    `connection.request.approved` and `connection.request.declined`,
    with their `ref`s. §10.9 feed kinds: the seven kinds the vault
    creates that no list named, `vault.pin_changed`,
    `device.secret_renewed`, `credential.recovered`,
    `recovery.device_paired`, `recovery.completed`,
    `identity.rotation_failed` and `identity.rotate_conflict`, and the
    three that only §11.14.11 named, `recovery.attempt`,
    `recovery.change_required` and `recovery.counter_unavailable`.
    §11.14.11: `recovery.attempt`'s `ref` is
    `<generation>/<n>/<outcome>/counter`, the outcome in the `ref` (no
    `outcome` or `source` members); an attempt is written again when it
    later succeeds; the details a host can drop are their own
    `recovery.open` entries (never `ok`), which the apps match to
    attempts by time, since attempts carry no `recovery_id`;
    `recovery.generation_closed`'s `/unconfirmed` suffix;
    `recovery.completed` also has the `ref` `<recovery_id>/resumed`;
    `recovery.change_required`'s `ref`. The export example's label
    follows the renamed title
  - 0.49.0: normative, owner decision of 2026-10-19 (approved by the
    owner (2026-10-19)); revised after review. §11.5,
    §11.11.4, §11.14.6, §11.14.8: **a recovery cancelled by an unlock
    reaches the member API**, and **a cancel names its recovery**.
    (1) The answer to an `unlock` whose sealed result is `{ok: true,
    recovery_cancelled: true}` carries the clear marker `code:
    "recovery_cancelled"` with `cancelled_recovery_id`, the id of the
    recovery it ended; the parent copies both into the unlock's slot. As
    a backstop for an answer lost between the enclave and the slot, the
    `unlocked` lifecycle event of that unlock carries the same id, and
    the parent writes it to the vault row (`recovery_cancelled`). The
    member API ends the recovery with that id as `cancelled`, once,
    from either source, and emails the member (MEMBER-API 2.9.0).
    Until now the account site kept showing such a recovery as
    pending, and a new request was answered `409 recovery_active`.
    (2) Approved by the owner (2026-10-19): a
    signed `recovery_cancel` carries the `recovery_id` it means, inside
    the signature, and the enclave cancels only that recovery; an older
    release keeps "whatever is in progress". Both need a vault release
    (the enclave and its parent) as well as the member API: the host
    cannot read the sealed result, so only the enclave can say what was
    cancelled. VAULT-HOST-PROTOCOL 0.1.13 follows
  - 0.48.0: normative, owner decision of 2026-10-19 (vettid.org #358
    part 1); no vault release. §11.14.9 **"A lost answer to
    `credential.reset`"** replaces "`credential.reset` is not covered
    here": a reset that applied without its answer reaching the phone
    left the vault at version 1 under a new key while the phone held
    blob N, so the phone's next credential operation was taken for a
    clone. The reset is now sent as a change is: nothing else in flight,
    the version pre-check (whose `key` the app records), an `exp`, the
    same request resent while it has not expired; it is decided by
    `credential.version` (another `key` or a lower `version` is
    applied: fetch, keep, acknowledge, top up UTKs; the same `key` and
    `version` after the margin is not applied), and every other
    credential operation waits for the decision. vettid-vault staging
    release 18 already has what it needs (`key` in `credential.version`,
    `exp` checked before the dedupe, every answer of a reset cached under
    its id). §3.5.5 points to it. ANDROID-PLAN 0.1.51 and IOS-PLAN 0.1.9
    follow; both apps keep "New credential" hidden until they implement
    it
  - 0.47.1: clarifications, owner decisions of 2026-10-19 (vettid.org
    #358 part 2); no vault release. §11.14.9 "Sent with the vault's
    current blob": (a) no answer to the `credential.version` pre-check
    is shown with the app's plain "can't reach the service" text, not a
    "change pending" text, since nothing was sent (0.47.0 named the
    "can't reach" text of an unresolved change); (b) an error answer, an
    answer without a version, or `exists: false` counts as "differs":
    the app fetches, and refuses with the "earlier request" text unless
    the fetched blob is the vault's current one; the head of the next
    bullet ("Besides the candidate record …"), lost in 0.47.0, is
    restored. §3.5.9 "Forced rotation": (c) what the vault answers a
    holder that presents a superseded blob during an alarm (vettid-vault
    staging release 18), when the holder asks `credential.version`
    (before a rotation while an alarm is open, and on a rotation
    answered `rotation_required` or `credential_frozen`), and that it
    fetches and retries the rotation once when the version or the key
    differs; a whole-phone copy with the same device id that knows the
    password can finish the rotation first, and the vault cannot tell
    the two copies apart. ANDROID-PLAN 0.1.50 and IOS-PLAN 0.1.8 follow
  - 0.47.0: normative, approved by the owner 2026-10-19 (vettid.org #347); no
    vault release. §11.14.9 "A lost answer" step 1: (1) **sent with the
    vault's current blob**: right before a change or a renew, inside the
    serialization that sends credential operations and once every
    earlier request is settled, the app asks `credential.version`. When
    it differs from the blob the request would carry, the app fetches
    the latest blob and sends with it, or refuses with nothing sent.
    Without this check, an earlier operation that applied without its
    answer (an owner check, a name change, `credential.unlock`,
    `credential.rotate`, a transfer's approval) would make step 3 read
    its version step as the change. The assumption about the vault (one
    batch at a time, in mailbox order, nothing while locked) is stated.
    (2) A renew's own refusal, `stale_credential` included, decides it
    not applied; only a renew with no answer is decided by
    `credential.version`. ANDROID-PLAN 0.1.48 and IOS-PLAN 0.1.6 follow
  - 0.46.1: normative; **approved by the owner 2026-10-18**; corrects
    0.46.0's scope of failed checks (§3.6.1): only operations that
    verify the PIN as an owner check does count a wrong PIN or password
    as a failed check (`credential.create`, `pin.change`,
    `vault.secret.renew`, `credential.password.change`,
    `credential.reset`, `device.transfer.approve`, `vault.delete`);
    operations that test the password alone (unlocking or rotating the
    credential, item and feature operations, `credential.recover`)
    count only in the password backoff, and `audit.export`'s PIN only in
    its own backoff (§10.9). `vault.delete` and
    `device.transfer.approve` check the blob before the PIN (§6.7.1,
    §12.5). Implemented in vettid-vault #123 (needs a vault release)
  - 0.46.0: normative; **approved by the owner 2026-10-18**; **needs a
    vault release** (staging) for (1). (1) **Failed checks**: in
    `credential.password.change` a `bad_pin` and a `bad_password` each
    count as a failed owner check (§3.6.4), and so in every credential
    operation that tests the PIN or the password; a request refused
    before any secret is tested counts nothing (§3.6.1, §11.14.9).
    (2) **A renew is settled before a PIN change** (§11.14.9 "A lost
    answer" step 1): an unanswered `vault.secret.renew` is recorded
    before sending and decided by `credential.version`; while it could
    still apply a PIN change is refused, and when the version cannot
    decide, the app offers a lock and unlock, which costs nothing because
    the PIN has not changed. Step 5's "other candidates first" stays only
    as the fallback. (3) **Settled on answers only**: a pending
    credential request is settled by its answer or by the `ts` of a
    vault answer, not by other vault messages; one `credential.version`
    may be sent to obtain a vault time. (4) **"Finish the move"** is one
    of the lock-and-unlock flows refused while a change is unresolved or
    a PIN uncertain; only step 5's two-step prompts send a PIN with a
    candidate. ANDROID-PLAN 0.1.47 and IOS-PLAN 0.1.5 follow
  - 0.45.0: normative, approved by the owner 2026-10-18; corrects and completes
    0.44.0's "A lost answer" (§11.14.9). A minor version rather than a
    patch, because it adds app rules and a vault order of checks;
    **needs a vault release** for that order only. (1) Step 4: a
    `stale_credential` to the change means **this change did not
    apply**. The vault caches that answer under the request's id, so no
    copy can apply later. The app no longer decides by
    `credential.version` then, because the version moved for the earlier
    operation. (2) Step 5: `ok` with the previous PIN **does not decide**
    the change; a queued copy can still apply until `exp`, and the check
    after the unlock decides. (3) Step 1: a change is sent only with **no
    other credential operation queued or awaiting its answer** (wait up
    to 30 s, else refuse), and the stored marker refuses a second change.

    after `device_secret`, for the new PIN with the candidate, so that

  - 0.36.0: normative; approved by the owner 2026-10-17 (owner decisions of
    2026-10-17); follows 0.35.0; no enclave change and no vault release
    (the vault accepts any 32-byte `unlock_secret`). **Android's

    (§11.14.1): 32 random bytes `r` per epoch, mixed into the HMAC
    message under the new label `vettid/vms/2/unlock-secret-2` with the
    same Keystore key, and stored with the epoch in one atomic write of
    the account record, so that code that ran as the app can no longer
    compute the secret of an epoch created after it stopped running. The
    formula names `key_vault` (the vault id, or `""` after a transfer),
    as the app always computed it. Rules for records and lost answers:
    store before send; reuse on automatic retries; a new change makes a
    new candidate and keeps the unconfirmed ones, at most four, and a
    fifth change is refused until the member unlocks; confirmation only
    by the operation's answer or by the existing rule during an unlock
    (`ok`, `bad_pin`, `transfer_incomplete` after `device_secret`), and
    an `ok` with the current record ends the candidates; the current
    record is never dropped on another answer; replaced records deleted
    7 days after a later epoch is confirmed; an explicit "try the earlier
    secret" step, offered only while a replaced record exists and never
    automatic, moved only by `ok` (or `transfer_incomplete`), never by
    `bad_pin`, and followed by a History entry and a new phone secret,
    for an operator restore of §11.14.2; a failed or dropped record write
    stops the operation before anything is sent; at epoch 1 the key, then
    the record, then the request; only a definite loss of the phone key
    or the account record counts as lost keys; an app refuses to start on
    an account record whose format it does not know, writing and wiping
    nothing. Staging phones keep
    their form 1 record, with no prompt, until their next renew, PIN
    change or new phone key. Corrected: §11.14.1 "What the secret
    protects against", §11.14.9 (`vault.secret.renew`), §11.14.12 and
    the §13.5 row "The phone's unlock secret", which said that a renew or
    a PIN change ends any exposure; on Android before this change, code
    that ran as the app could compute later epochs in advance and only a

    names the earlier secret; §16 gains the `phone_2` vectors, with
    values. ANDROID-PLAN 0.1.43 follows
  - 0.35.0: normative, additive; **approved by the owner 2026-10-17**

    key-agreement key per `key_vault` (`privateKeyUsage`,
    `WhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly`, not synchronizable, not bound to

    whose private half is dropped after a key confirmation at creation;
    `unlock_secret` = HKDF-SHA-256 over the 32-byte x-coordinate, with
    both public keys (SEC1 uncompressed) in `info` under the label
    `vettid/vms/2/unlock-secret-ios`; a 16-byte check tag for the

    epoch is stored before the request that carries its secret, reused
    on a retry, kept as a candidate while its answer is lost and tried
    after a `device_secret` answer; replaced records deleted 7 days
    after a later epoch is confirmed (a clock set back never extends
    this) or at a wipe, and tried only from an explicit step the member
    takes, as on Android (0.36.0, §11.14.1 rule 7); never in purgeable
    storage. First-run cleanup of the

    period, no software key in release or staging builds, and why the
    alternatives were not chosen. A locked iPhone is never treated as
    lost keys ("Unlock your iPhone", then a retry); with four
    unconfirmed candidates a new change is refused until an unlock,
    never by dropping one. The protection class is stricter than
    Android's rule, decided by the owner; `AfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly`
    and its residual are recorded as not chosen. "Missing" counts only when protected
    data is available before and after the lookup and the lookup itself
    answers not found; the first-run cleanup reads a marker file and
    runs only while protected data is available; typed secrets are
    dropped when the screen locks. §11.7, §11.14's summary, §15 item 39
    and §16 (the `phone_ios` vectors, with values) follow. Nothing

  - 0.34.0: release R (0.33.0); **approved by the owner 2026-10-16**
    (vettid.org #311; owner decisions of 2026-10-16: the name
    `capabilities`; `recovery_offered` listed only when the release
    offers recovery; a vault without `recovery_r` keeps its release's
    earlier recovery). (1) **`attempt_used`**: every
    `vault.recovery.open.result` says whether that request used one of
    the ten attempts (`true` exactly when the counter answered `spent`
    or `lost` for it), so that the app no longer infers it from `code`,
    `attempts` or `retry_at` (§11.14.6). (2) **Release capabilities**
    (new §11.10.9): a release from R names the protocol capabilities it
    implements, `recovery_r` and `attachments`, as a constant of its
    image, in its **ETK descriptor** (§11.2), which its attestation
    binds, and in a **transfer's bundle** (§6.4, §6.7.1), which the
    QR's hash binds. The app reads them before it chooses the enroll,
    unlock, transfer or recovery path; a descriptor or bundle without
    them is a release before R. The app remembers per vault that it has
    seen `recovery_r` and from then on never uses a path from before R
    for that vault (§11.10.6). Neither the host, the member API nor the
    relay can add or remove a name, and the vault refuses every request
    of the shape before R, so a false or missing list can only make a
    request fail, never weaken it. The release number still comes from
    the manifest entry that the attested PCRs match (§11.10.1). (3) A
    channel's manifest has exactly one `active` release, and the one that
    makes a release with `recovery_r` active deprecates every older one,
    so that a first enrollment cannot be steered to a release without R
    (§11.10.9; enforced by vettid.org's manifest checks). (4) A bundle
    of another kind with `capabilities` is refused. (5) `recovery_offered`
    is listed exactly when the release's measured `recovery_offered` is
    `true`; without it beside `recovery_r` the app hides recovery. (6) **A
    lost `ok` is resumed** (owner decision of 2026-10-16): until the
    recovered phone's first handshake completes, that phone's own
    `vault.unlock` (its unlock secret and the PIN) carries `vault_bundle`
    and a fresh token again, repeatably, with no attempt used and no call
    to the counter (§11.4, §11.14.6). `attempt_used` is
    `true` if and only if the spend happened, `vault_missing` included.
    ANDROID-PLAN 0.1.41 follows
  - 0.33.2: release R (0.33.0): **the attempt counter's lock period is

  - 0.33.0: normative once approved; **wording for the owner's
    approval** (owner decisions of 2026-10-13 to 2026-10-15, the open

    30 days, each counted before it is tested **at an attempt counter
    outside everything the host stores** (S3 objects under Object Lock
    in compliance mode, VAULT-HOST-PROTOCOL §8.1) and checked again right
    after against the attempt's own time; a **72-hour quiet period**
    since the member was last present; a new generation (ten new
    attempts) at every change of PIN or password, and none until a
    change after ten used; the code valid across waits; every attempt in
    History and by email (`recovery_attempt`). **Every unlock needs a
    secret that only the phone's hardware can produce** (a non-exportable

    **replaced at every change of PIN, password or phone**, written in

    carry both secrets so that recovery is armed at once; new
    `vault.secret.renew`. New passwords: 12 characters, not common, a
    guessability estimate of 10^10, NFC. Recovery requests are signed by
    the member API (§11.11.2's open question, decided). A completed
    recovery rotates the vault's long-lived keys; a connection keeps the
    first successor of an identity key (§3.4). Transfers carry the new
    phone's secret and the password-and-PIN approval makes a new
    `opener`, the app key is reported pending at the first header write;
    the old phone deletes its keys at the new phone's first unlock from
    storage or 7 days after the approval, whichever comes first. A
    stored state and header that do not belong together are refused
    `stored_mismatch` before an attempt is spent; the state object names
    its `dek_version` in the clear (format 0x02). The old recovery path (`credential.recover`, the

    counter group (release "R3") are specified later; production

    §10.5.1 and §15 item 38
  - 0.32.0: normative; **approved by the owner 2026-10-15**
    (vettid.org #288: owner decisions of 2026-10-15, and the open
    questions as the coordinator recommended, §15 item 38); **needs a
    vault release** (the placeholder "release A") and an app release.
    Every rule it adds is marked "0.32.0, release A" (or "0.32.0" for
    the rules that apply to every message) and binds nothing before
    then. As approved: attachments are **app-only** (desktops and
    agents neither send nor fetch them; agents do not learn that a
    message has one); a recipient's full store reaches the sender only
    as a generic refusal; device tokens carry `owner_device` so that
    each mailbox keeps room for one blob from the owner's own devices
    (§7.1; RELAY-PROTOCOL 0.9.2). **Photo attachments** (new §10.5.1): one attachment
    per message, a photo of at most about 8 MiB (the relay's
    `max_blob_bytes`); the phone uploads it to its own vault, which
    stores a copy and sends a fresh one to the connection's vault,
    which stores its own; phones fetch on demand
    (`message.attachment.get`) and keep nothing. New types
    `message.attachment.get`, `.discard`, `.deliver` and `.status`;
    `attachment` on `message.send` and `message.new`; `message.send`
    is answered once its checks pass and the attachment's progress
    follows as `sync.event`. At-rest format and object keys; an index
    in vault state, created in the same flush as its message, objects
    written after it; the relay mailbox's shared blob storage (§1.2):
    blobs deleted once fetched, good or bad, uploads only on the
    recipient's request once that storage is full, orphans purged;
    a 1 GiB store per vault, 4,096 attachments, 256 MiB per
    connection; per-connection limits (§7.3); 2 transfers per vault
    and an instance admission by available memory (at most 4 until
    measured); held and locked behaviour; a 7-day window after which
    the sender is told, and fresh uploads on the recipient's `missing`
    within 30 days, asked for only when the recipient's mailbox has
    room, with a backoff and in turn across a connection's waiting
    attachments, and answered `withdrawn` when the sender will not
    upload; device and peer blobs deleted only after the content is
    stored; agents send and fetch none; connections removed or
    stale; deletion; audit and feed kinds (§10.9), `limit` names, the
    error code `response_too_large` and a `sync.event` kind (§10.1),
    storage use in `vault.status` (§10.2). §5.5: **the blob layout
    gains a version byte and Padmé padding with the length inside**,
    before anything uses it, with vectors (§16). §7.2: a token after
    `quota_exceeded`, the old one denylisted; §8.6 tells the token's
    quota from the mailbox's. §8.1: **a response that cannot be sealed
    is answered `response_too_large`, never silence**; §8.2:
    `message.list`, `message.get` and `message.attachment.get` are
    volatile. §12.5 erases attachments by their recorded versions,
    every convergence path reports `deleted`, and the parent sweeps
    the prefix after it (VAULT-HOST-PROTOCOL 0.1.9). **Also
    a gap closed for every message** (new §10.5.2): `message.list`
    pages are at most 131,072 bytes and continue with `before` and
    `next_before`; until now a long conversation's list could not fit
    §5.5, and the vault as built then sent no answer

    the app creates or accepts connections.** `action.respond{approve:
    true}` from a desktop or an agent is answered `forbidden`, whether

    its type became app-only is answered `forbidden` when an app
    approves it. Before, the invitation and introduction types were
    step-up types for desktops and `connection.approve` was open to
    them. A desktop may still decline (`connection.decline`,
    `intro.decline`) and deny. A desktop app hides the actions it
    cannot take. §3.1, §6.4 "Who approves", §6.8, §10.4, §10.14 (the

  - 0.30.0: normative, as built in vettid-vault #83; approved by the

  - 0.29.0: normative; **approved by the owner 2026-10-12** (vettid.org

    vault release**
    (the placeholder "release L") and a member API deploy. Every rule
    it adds is marked "0.29.0, release L" and binds nothing before
    then. **A lock belongs to its unlock**: each open makes an
    `unlock_id` (random, in memory only), carried in the unlock and
    enroll results and in `vault.status` (§11.4, §11.3, §10.2);

    through its durable outbox (§8.6). **Through the member API** the

    unlock, and the enclave answers after the lock with what happened:
    `locked`, `not_running` or `stale` (§11.5). **The idle lock**
    (new §3.6.8; §12.3; setting `idle_lock.after_seconds`, §10.8): a
    vault that is past its owner-check deadline by that long (7 days by
    default) locks itself; `vault.locking{reason: "idle"}`,

  - 0.28.0: normative; **approved by the owner 2026-10-12** (vettid.org
    #243: D12–D22 and D24–D26 as recommended; D23 as (c), the app never
    pins a connection's identity key itself); **needs a
    vault release** (staging "release C2", CALLS-PLAN 0.1.3 §13) and a
    host stack deploy. Calls, phase C2 (CALLS-PLAN V1, V2, V3, V5, V6,
    V8 and what phase C1 found; owner decisions of 2026-10-11 and
    2026-10-12, CALLS-PLAN §9 and §12, and D12–D26 of §13.5).
    §10.10 is rewritten around what S10 runs and what C2 adds, each
    C2 rule marked. **Servers and credentials** in the signed ICE
    configuration: the shared secret never enters a vault; the vault
    fetches short-lived TURN credentials from the calling service's
    issuer with an attestation and a key made for the one request,
    keeps a pool of 4 in memory and uses one per call (new release
    constant `calls_url`, §11.10.8). **A ring timer in the vault**: an
    unanswered call ends at its `exp` and the missed call is recorded
    by the vault. **Liveness**: `call.keepalive` every 30 s from the
    call's device, the call ended after 90 s without one. **Glare**:
    the lower `call_id` wins and one call connects. **Permission and
    limits**: calls allowed or off per connection
    (`call.permission.set`, `.list`), a limit on unanswered calls,
    merged missed calls. **`call.list`** gains `v`, `now`, `exp` and
    `device_id`. **Media suites as signed members** of both shares
    (form 2: `suites`, `suite`, `offered`; the exact bytes signed) and
    **key confirmation** before microphone audio (`confirm`), with the
    rules that keep S10's unsigned form from weakening a call while
    both exist, and when that form is retired. **Media suites and
    keys** lifted from vettid-android `docs/calls/CALL-MEDIA.md`
    unchanged: the registry, the SDP attributes, the direction keys,
    the frame cryptor's options, the frame key, the encrypted frame,
    the rules for a device. What each party sees and can do after C2;
    the residual (a member's own vault) is unchanged. **As built,
    corrected:** at S10 the ICE list is empty and devices have host
    candidates only (the text said "host and server-reflexive");
    `call.ice` is limited to 256 a call for both directions together;
    `call.start` also answers `owner_check_required` and `internal`;
    the issuer that held coturn's secret in the vault was never
    deployed and is withdrawn (§15 item 6 closed). (§8.5, §10, §10.1,
    §10.9, §10.10, §11.10.8, §15 items 6 and 36, §16)

  - 0.27.1: editorial-normative, errata to 0.26.0 and 0.27.0 from
    their implementations (vettid-vault #62, #63, #64, staging release
    S10; vettid-android #116; approved by the owner 2026-10-11, all five
    recommendations as drafted). No wire
    change. **Key attestation chain rules** (§11.7), enforced from S10:
    the attestation extension on the leaf only, CAs above the
    attestation certificate, path lengths, the attestation certificate
    itself not required to be a CA, 1–10 certificates, validity
    checked at an attestation. Background, plainly: until S10 the
    enclave checked each signature up to the pinned root and read the
    extension from the first certificate, so **a chain extended below
    a genuinely attested key was accepted** as the attestation of
    another key. An independent review found it on 2026-10-11 and it
    was fixed the same day (vettid-vault #64, S10, `security: urgent`).
    It never bypassed the PIN, the credential password, a transfer's
    approval or the recovery code. **A phone whose attestation
    certificates have expired cannot attach a vault** (owner decision
    2026-10-11). Chains seen on the test phones. **Signer binding as
    built** (§11.7.1): the staging exception is derived from the
    measured channel and release, not a constant; the old class in
    `device.signer_changed` when the old signer is no longer pinned; a
    wrong `signer` in an approval is always `signer_unconfirmed`;
    changed by digest, confirmed by class; transfers across
    platforms; the same digest listed twice is refused;
    `signer_refused` is decided before `recovery_pending` and
    `backoff`, and what follows from that; its log entry (24 hours,
    not on a rolled-back header, the shared 64 entries); a bind by
    chain re-runs every check but the challenge and validity, is kept
    even when the PIN then fails, and its size limit; `device_id` on
    `device.signer_bound`; a registered recovery has no expiry in the
    vault; the real-phone test replaced by what was run at S10 (no
    staging vault can bind by chain). **Release check** (§11.10.8):
    "previous release" is the highest lower tag, and rule 2 runs in
    the release workflow. The same-phone transfer by pasted code
    among the ways to move a staging vault. 0.25.0 and 0.26.0 marked
    approved. **Owner decisions (2026-10-11, all as recommended):**
    the vault will keep the last recorded Android signer across an
    app without one (decided; built in 0.55.9, vettid-vault #142); a
    vault attached while its certificates were valid keeps unlocking; the consequences of `signer_refused`'s order are
    accepted as built; confirmation stays by class (§11.7.1, §15
    item 35) (§10.9, §11.7, §11.7.1, §11.10.8, §15
    item 35; ANDROID-PLAN 0.1.37)
  - 0.27.0: normative; an enclave change and a vault release (owner
    decision of 2026-10-11, ANDROID-PLAN 0.1.36: the Play app-signing
    key is Google's and VettID's release key is never given to Google;
    §15 item 35; approved by the owner 2026-10-11, all eight
    recommendations as drafted): **per-vault signer
    binding** on Android. Until now a vault accepted an app whose
    attestation showed any signing certificate the release pins, and
    did not keep which. Now the digest is recorded with the attested
    device key at enrollment, transfer and recovery; unlock and a
    release-update approval require the recorded signer to be pinned
    by the running release (`signer_refused`: sealed, not a PIN
    failure, audited, no alarm); the binding changes only by a direct
    transfer, where a change of signer is shown to the holder and must
    be confirmed in the approval (`signer_unconfirmed`), or by a
    completed recovery, each audited as `device.signer_changed` with
    the old and new class; vaults enrolled earlier bind from the
    certificate chain of the key they enrolled with
    (`device_assertion.chain`); an attestation must report exactly one
    signing digest; pinned signers carry a class (`vettid`,
    `google_play`, `development`) in the release configuration, and
    the app's `device.list` entry reports `signer{class, digest}`.
    Android only; how it would extend to iOS (new §11.7.1; §6.7.1,
    §10.3, §10.9, §11.3, §11.4, §11.7, §11.9, §11.10.8, §11.11.3,
    §11.11.5, §15 item 35; ANDROID-PLAN 0.1.36, VAULT-RELEASES 0.1.12).

  - 0.25.0: normative, additive; no enclave change and no vault release
    (owner decision of 2026-10-11, "we should allow a typed recovery
    code"; §15 item 33; approved by the owner 2026-10-11, merged as
    vettid.org #212): the recovery
    code can be **typed** when the new phone cannot scan the portal's
    QR. The portal shows one string of 48 Crockford characters in 12
    groups of four: a 12-character **locator** minted by the member API
    (60 random bits; it stands for the QR's `vault_id` and
    `recovery_id` and opens nothing), the 32-character code unchanged,
    and 4 **check characters** computed in the browser over the
    portal's `api` origin, the locator and the code. The app verifies
    the check with its own origin before anything is sent (a typing
    mistake, or a code of another environment's site, is caught on the
    phone and is not a wrong code), claims by locator
    (`POST /api/vault/recovery/claim {locator, app_key}`, answered with
    `vault_id` and `recovery_id`), and from there registers exactly as
    after a scan: the same sealed register, the same answers, the same
    5 wrong codes, the same 24 hours, single use, PIN and credential
    password. The bare 32-character text the portal showed "for typing"
    is withdrawn (no app could use it since 0.15.0) (§11.11,
    §11.11.2, §11.11.3, §11.11.6, §11.11.7, §11.11.8, new §11.11.10,
    §13.5, §15 item 33, §16; MEMBER-API 2.4.0, ANDROID-PLAN 0.1.33)
  - 0.24.1: editorial-normative, errata to 0.24.0 from its
    implementation (vettid-vault #59, N3; approved, owner decision

    event is `push.token-needed` (0.24.0's `push.token_needed` broke
